chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah (Exalted is His Glory) said:
One who humiliates My friend has prepared for a battle with Me.
And My servant has never drawn closer to Me with anything better than what I have made obligatory on him; and indeed, he draws closer to Me with supererogatory actions until I love him.
And when I love him, I become his ears that he hears with, his eyes that he sees with, his hands that he grasps with and his legs that he walks with.
If he calls upon Me, I answer him; and if he asks from Me, I grant him.
There is nothing I hesitate in doing like in taking the life of a believer. He dislikes death and I dislike causing him pain.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a believer who performs supererogatory acts according to Hadith Qudsi?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in *Kitab al-Mumin*, outlines the spiritual hierarchy of divine proximity, beginning with the fulfillment of obligatory duties (fara'id) and ascending through supererogatory acts (nawafil) to the state of 'Divine Love' (mahabbah). In this exalted state, God becomes the believer's sensory faculties, ensuring their actions are divinely guided, while demonstrating a unique divine hesitation in the believer's death due to mutual affection. The narration underscores the Shia concept of 'Ishq' (passionate love) as the ultimate goal of worship, where the believer's will aligns seamlessly with the Divine Will.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 62. It has been related that Abu Ja'far (a.s): Allah [M.G] has said:
One who humiliates My friend has prepared for a battle with Me.
And a servant has never drawn close to Me with anything better than what I have made obligatory on him; and indeed, he draws closer to Me with supererogatory actions until I love him.
And when I love him, I become his ears that he hears with, his eyes that he sees with, his hands that he grasps with and his legs that he walks with.
If he calls upon Me, I answer him; and if He asks from Me, I grant him.
There is nothing I hesitate in doing like in taking the life of a believer. He dislikes death and I dislike causing him pain.
